# Paid Time Off (PTO) Policy

## Overview

Meridian Health Partners provides all full-time employees with 15 days of paid time off annually. This policy applies to all employees in Claims Ops, Care Coordination, Data & Analytics, Platform Engineering, and HR across all office locations.

## Accrual and Year Definition

PTO accrues on a calendar year basis (January 1 – December 31). Employees receive their full 15-day allocation on January 1st each year. This applies to new hires as well, prorated to their start date.

**Example:** An employee hired on July 15th receives 7.5 days of PTO for that calendar year (50% of 15 days).

## Requesting PTO

All PTO requests must be submitted through Workday at least 14 days in advance. Requests are submitted to your direct manager for approval.

**Process:**
1. Open Workday and navigate to Time Off
2. Select "PTO Request"
3. Choose dates and enter reason (optional)
4. Submit for manager approval
5. You will receive email confirmation once approved

For urgent requests with less than 14 days' notice, email your manager directly and follow up in Workday.

## Blackout Dates and Restrictions

Certain periods have restricted PTO availability due to business needs:

- **Month-end close (last 5 business days of each month):** Claims Ops team members cannot take PTO
- **Q4 planning period (October 1-15):** Data & Analytics team members cannot take PTO
- **Holiday weeks:** Thanksgiving week and the week of December 24-28 require manager approval and are limited to 2 employees per team per day

## Use-It-or-Lose-It Policy

Unused PTO does not carry over to the next calendar year. All 15 days must be used by December 31st or they are forfeited. Managers are responsible for encouraging their teams to use PTO throughout the year.

## Holidays

Meridian Health Partners observes 10 company holidays annually (separate from PTO). These include New Year's Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Thanksgiving, and Christmas. Holiday schedules are posted in Confluence by November 1st each year.

## PTO During Separation

If an employee leaves Meridian Health Partners, unused PTO is not paid out except where required by state law. Employees should coordinate their final PTO dates with their manager and HR during the offboarding process.

## PTO During Separation

## Medical Leave

Extended medical leave beyond 15 days of PTO should be discussed with HR. Short-term disability and other leave options may be available. Contact the HR team in Slack channel #hr-support.

## Questions and Updates

Questions about PTO should be directed to your manager or HR. This policy is reviewed annually and updates will be posted in Confluence. The last update to this policy was April 2023.

# Paid Time Off (PTO) Policy Update – Effective January 1, 2025

## Overview

Meridian Health Partners is updating the company-wide PTO policy effective January 1, 2025. All employees now receive **20 days of paid time off per year**, regardless of tenure or role. This supersedes the 2024 PTO policy and applies to all full-time employees across all departments.

## PTO Allocation

**Annual Entitlement:** 20 days per calendar year (160 hours for full-time employees)

- Days are allocated on January 1st each year
- Part-time employees receive prorated PTO based on their scheduled hours
- New hires receive prorated PTO based on their start date (calculated as: 20 days × months remaining in calendar year ÷ 12)

*Example: An employee starting March 15, 2025 receives approximately 10.5 days for 2025.*

## Requesting and Approval

1. **Submit requests in Workday** under Time Off → PTO Request minimum 2 weeks in advance
2. **Notify your direct manager** via Slack or email for same-week requests (not guaranteed approval)
3. **Managers must approve/deny within 48 hours** of submission
4. Cross-team coverage coordination is the responsibility of the requesting employee's manager

For Claims Ops and Care Coordination teams, please coordinate with your team leads to ensure adequate staffing. Contact your department head if conflicts arise.

## Carryover and Payout

- **No carryover permitted** – unused PTO does not roll into the following year
- Employees must use their 20 days within the calendar year (January 1 – December 31)
- Upon termination, employees receive payout for unused PTO at their current rate of pay
- Payout is processed through Workday payroll within the final paycheck

## Sick Leave

Sick leave is **separate from PTO** and is managed independently. Sick leave requests should be submitted in Workday and communicated to your manager as soon as possible (ideally before your shift).

## Holidays

Company holidays (11 days annually) are **separate from PTO**. See the 2025 Holiday Calendar posted in Confluence by HR.

## Remote and Hybrid Considerations

Employees working remotely or on hybrid schedules follow the same PTO policy. Out-of-office status must be set in Slack and your Workday calendar.

## Remote and Hybrid Considerations

## Questions and Support

- **HR:** Contact hr@meridianhealth.com or post in #hr-general on Slack
- **Workday issues:** Submit tickets to the IT Help Desk via #platform-support
- **Manager questions:** Escalate to your department head

## Policy Effective Date

This policy takes effect **January 1, 2025** and replaces all prior PTO policies from 2024 and earlier.

# Expense Reimbursement Policy

## Policy Overview

Meridian Health Partners reimburses reasonable business expenses incurred by employees in the course of their work. All reimbursement requests must be submitted within 30 days of expense date. Expenses submitted after 90 days will not be reimbursed.

## Expense Categories and Limits

### Travel

- **Airfare**: Coach/economy class only. Exceptions require VP approval.
- **Mileage**: $0.67 per mile (IRS standard rate). Use Workday mileage calculator.
- **Rental cars**: Mid-size or smaller. Weekly rates preferred over daily.
- **Lodging**: $150/night limit (major metros: $200/night). Includes taxes.
- **Meals while traveling**: $60/day limit. Alcoholic beverages capped at $15 per meal.

### Office & Professional

- **Software/tools**: Pre-approval required for purchases over $500. Contact Platform Engineering.
- **Conference registration**: Up to $2,500 without approval. Above $2,500 requires director sign-off.
- **Professional development**: Books, courses, certifications up to $1,000/year per employee.
- **Office supplies**: Coordinate through HR. Personal reimbursement only if urgent.

### Client/Business Meals

- **Client entertainment**: $75/person limit. Requires business purpose documentation.
- **Team meals**: $30/person limit for working lunches. Requires attendee list.

## Submission Process

1. **Collect receipts**: Keep original receipts for all expenses over $25. Digital copies acceptable (photograph or PDF).
2. **Log in Workday**: Enter expense details under "Reimbursement Requests" module. Attach receipt images.
3. **Add business purpose**: One-sentence explanation of business purpose required for all expenses.
4. **Manager approval**: Submit to direct manager for review and approval in Workday.
5. **Finance processing**: After manager approval, Finance team processes within 5-7 business days.
6. **Payment**: Direct deposit to employee's registered bank account (same as payroll).

## Timeline Requirements

- **Submission deadline**: 30 days from expense date
- **Manager review SLA**: 3 business days
- **Finance processing**: 5-7 business days after manager approval
- **Payment window**: 10-14 business days from original submission

*Note: Expenses submitted 31-90 days after incurrence may be reimbursed at manager's discretion but are not guaranteed.*

- Traffic violations, parking tickets, or vehicle damage
- Home internet or phone bills (unless explicitly approved as remote work equipment)
- Alcoholic beverages for non-client meals
- Childcare or pet care

## Special Approvals

**Questions?** Contact HR at hr@meridianhealth.com or Finance at reimbursement@meridianhealth.com. Most FAQs are documented in Confluence under "Finance Policies."

# Remote Work and Hybrid Schedule Policy

**Effective Date:** January 15, 2023  
**Last Updated:** March 2024  
**Policy Owner:** HR Department

## Overview

Meridian Health Partners supports flexible work arrangements for eligible employees. This policy outlines guidelines for remote work and hybrid schedules across our 900-person organization.

## Eligibility

All full-time employees are eligible for remote or hybrid work arrangements, with the following exceptions:

- Claims Ops staff processing high-volume claims must maintain at least 3 days/week in-office
- Care Coordination team members require minimum 2 days/week on-site for patient-facing interactions
- Platform Engineering may work fully remote with manager approval
- Data & Analytics roles are flexible (typically 1-2 days on-site)

Contractors and temporary employees must confirm remote eligibility with HR before arrangement begins.

## Hybrid Schedule Options

**Option A (2-3 Days On-Site):** Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday in office. Monday and Friday flexible.

**Option B (1-2 Days On-Site):** Designated days determined by team lead. Must align with core collaboration hours (Tuesday-Thursday 10am-3pm ET).

**Full Remote:** Available for Data & Analytics, Platform Engineering, and select HR roles. Requires VP-level approval and 6-month probationary period.

## Work-From-Home Guidelines

**Equipment:** Meridian provides laptop, monitor, and keyboard. Internet stipend of $50/month for home office setup (submit receipt to Workday).

**VPN & Security:** All remote work requires VPN connection. Never access ClaimsFlow, CareBridge, or PulseBoard on public networks.

**Workspace:** Maintain a quiet, professional environment for video calls. No background video calls from vehicles or public spaces.

**Availability:** Remote employees must maintain posted office hours in Slack and respond to messages within 2 hours during business hours (8am-6pm ET).

## Scheduling and Approval

1. Discuss arrangement with direct manager
2. Complete Remote Work Agreement form (Confluence template: HR/Remote-Work-Forms)
3. Submit to HR via Workday by the 15th of prior month
4. Approval typically within 5 business days

Changes to schedule require 2 weeks' notice. Emergency schedule changes must be approved by team lead same day.

3. Submit to HR via Workday by the 15th of prior month

## Collaboration Expectations

- Attend all mandatory all-hands meetings (currently Tuesdays 2pm ET)

- Participate in team standup meetings (see Jira calendar for times)
- Quarterly in-person team meetings required for all remote staff

- Monitor/keyboard/mouse (up to $300)
- Ergonomic chair (up to $400)
- Internet stipend: $50/month

# Code of Conduct Summary

## Purpose

This document outlines the core behavioral expectations for all Meridian Health Partners employees across all departments and locations. Our Code of Conduct supports our mission to improve healthcare outcomes while maintaining a respectful, professional workplace.

## Core Principles

All employees must adhere to the following principles:

- **Integrity**: Conduct business honestly and transparently in all interactions
- **Respect**: Treat colleagues, clients, and partners with dignity regardless of role or background
- **Compliance**: Follow all applicable healthcare regulations, company policies, and legal requirements
- **Accountability**: Take responsibility for your actions and decisions

## Professional Conduct Standards

### Workplace Behavior

- Maintain professional communication across all platforms (Slack, email, in-person meetings)
- Avoid harassment, discrimination, or hostile behavior based on protected characteristics
- Report concerns through your direct manager or HR (hr@meridianhealth.com)
- Dress code: Business casual in office settings; follow department guidelines for client meetings

### Confidentiality and Data Protection

- Never share patient health information (PHI) outside authorized channels
- All ClaimsFlow, CareBridge, and PulseBoard data must remain confidential
- Use secure passwords and enable two-factor authentication on all company systems
- Report suspected data breaches to Platform Engineering immediately (security@meridianhealth.com)
- Violations may result in termination and legal action

### Conflicts of Interest

- Disclose any financial interests, family relationships, or personal connections to colleagues or clients
- Do not solicit personal favors from business partners or vendors
- Avoid accepting gifts valued over $50 from external parties
- Report conflicts to your department head within 5 business days

## Social Media and External Communications

- Do not identify Meridian Health Partners clients or patient outcomes on personal social media
- Company social accounts are managed exclusively by Marketing
- Employees speaking publicly about company matters must receive written approval from Communications
- Personal opinions on social media should not represent company positions

## Social Media and External Communications

- Do not identify Meridian Health Partners clients or patient outcomes on personal social media
- Company social accounts are managed exclusively by Marketing
- Employees speaking publicly about company matters must receive written approval from Communications
- Personal opinions on social media should not represent company positions

## System and Tool Usage

- ClaimsFlow, CareBridge, TimeTrax, and all company systems are for business purposes only
- Limit personal use of company devices and Slack to minimal, reasonable breaks
- Do not attempt to access systems outside your authorized role or department
- GitHub commits must include meaningful messages and reference corresponding Jira tickets

## Violations and Consequences

Violations of this Code of Conduct may result in:

- Verbal warning (first minor offense)
- Written warning (second offense or serious first offense)
- Suspension (repeated violations)
- Termination (severe violations including fraud, data theft, or harassment)

All employees must complete Code of Conduct training annually. New hires complete training during onboarding with HR.

## Questions?

Contact Human Resources at hr@meridianhealth.com or visit the Code of Conduct page on Confluence (internal-policies/code-of-conduct).

# Security and Data Handling Policy

**Last Updated:** March 2024 | **Owner:** Platform Engineering

## Overview

All Meridian Health Partners employees must follow these security and data handling practices. This applies to work with ClaimsFlow, CareBridge, PulseBoard, TimeTrax, and any patient or claims data.

## Access Control

- Request system access through Jira ticket to Platform Engineering (use project key `INFRA-ACCESS`)
- Access is role-based. Claims Ops staff get ClaimsFlow + read-only PulseBoard. Care Coordination gets CareBridge only.
- Managers approve access requests within 3 business days
- Quarterly access reviews happen in January, April, July, and October. Confirm your access is still needed.
- Terminate access within 24 hours of employee departure (HR notifies Platform Engineering via Slack #offboarding channel)

## Password and Authentication

- All system passwords must be 12+ characters with uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and symbols
- Store passwords in 1Password (company vault). Do not use personal password managers.
- Enable multi-factor authentication (MFA) on all accounts. Use authenticator apps, not SMS when possible.
- Change passwords every 90 days. Set calendar reminders.
- Never share credentials. If you need to give someone temporary access, request it formally—don't share your login.

## Patient Data Handling

- Patient data includes names, medical record numbers, claim IDs, and health information in CareBridge
- Only access patient data needed for your job. Claims Ops doesn't need full medical histories; use claim summaries.
- Do not download patient data to personal devices or non-company laptops
- Screenshots containing patient data require approval from your manager and Data & Analytics. File requests in Confluence space `DATA-REQUESTS`
- Talking about specific patients outside work is prohibited, even with family members

## Remote Work and Devices

- Use company laptops only. Personal devices cannot access ClaimsFlow or CareBridge.
- Enable full disk encryption on your laptop (IT sets this up during onboarding)
- Lock your screen (Windows key + L) when stepping away, even for 2 minutes
- Use company VPN when working from coffee shops, airports, or home. VPN setup instructions are in Confluence under `IT-SETUP`
- Report lost or stolen laptops to IT immediately at security@meridianhealth.local

## Incident Reporting

- If you suspect a security breach, unauthorized access, or mishandled data, report it immediately to Platform Engineering in Slack (#security-incidents) or email security@meridianhealth.local
- Do not investigate on your own or tell colleagues before reporting
- Include: what happened, when, which systems/data, and who was involved
- Reports are treated confidentially

## Training

- Complete security training annually (assigned in Workday, due by December 31)
- New hires must complete training within first 30 days
- Care Coordination staff take additional HIPAA training every 18 months

## Questions?

Post in Slack #security-help or email security@meridianhealth.local. Platform Engineering responds within 1 business day.

# ClaimsFlow Standard Claim Processing Runbook

## Overview

This runbook covers the standard workflow for processing a routine medical claim in ClaimsFlow. Most claims follow this path; complex cases requiring manual review are handled separately (see "Escalation Procedures" in Confluence).

## Prerequisites

- Active ClaimsFlow login with Claims Ops role
- Access to member's insurance policy details in CareBridge
- Updated fee schedule (updated quarterly, last refresh: Q3 2024)

## Prerequisites

- Active ClaimsFlow login with Claims Ops role
- Access to member's insurance policy details in CareBridge
- Updated fee schedule (updated quarterly, last refresh: Q3 2024)

## Step-by-Step Process

### 1. Claim Receipt & Initial Validation

When a claim arrives via EDI or manual upload, it automatically lands in the **Intake Queue** dashboard. Claims appear with status "Received."

- Verify claim ID is unique (system prevents duplicates automatically)
- Check that provider NPI, member ID, and date of service are present
- If any field is missing, move to "Pending Information" and notify submitter via email

### 2. Eligibility Verification

- Click the member ID to pull up their active policy in CareBridge
- Confirm policy was active on the date of service (DOS)
- Check for any coverage exclusions or waiting periods
- If ineligible, reject claim with reason code "ELG-001" and notify member within 2 business days

### 3. Benefit Determination

- Navigate to the **Benefits Calculator** tab
- Input procedure code (CPT or HCPCS), DOS, and provider type
- System automatically applies deductible, copay, and coinsurance based on member's plan tier
- Review calculated member responsibility and insurance liability

**Example:** CPT 99213 (office visit) under Silver Plan = $40 copay + 20% coinsurance on remaining balance.

### 4. Adjudication

- Click "Adjudicate" button to apply fee schedule
- System compares billed amount against contracted rate (usually 80-120% of Medicare)
- Any variance >15% triggers automatic hold for manual review
- Assuming no flags, system calculates final approval amount

### 5. Claim Decision & Notification

Select one of three outcomes:

- **Approve:** Claim moves to payment queue; generates EOB within 24 hours
- **Deny:** Requires reason code (e.g., "NOT-CVG" for non-covered service); member receives denial notice
- **Request More Info:** Suspends claim; sends secure message to provider

### 6. Payment Processing

Approved claims move to **Payment Batch** status. Batches process nightly at 11 PM ET.

- Payments typically reach provider bank accounts within 2-3 business days
- Check TimeTrax for payment confirmation logs (available under Reports > Payment History)

## Common Issues

- **"Duplicate claim detected"** – Check if member already has claim for same DOS/provider/amount in last 30 days
- **Fee schedule mismatch** – Verify provider contract type in CareBridge; update if needed
- **Stuck in adjudication** – High-variance claims often require Claims Ops supervisor approval (Slack @claims-supervisors)

## Escalation

For claims exceeding $50K or involving workers' compensation, contact Data & Analytics team before adjudication.

# Handling a Rejected Claim - Runbook

## Overview

When a claim is rejected in ClaimsFlow, the Claims Ops team must investigate the root cause and take corrective action within 48 hours. Rejection reasons vary from missing documentation to coding errors to eligibility issues.

## Step 1: Identify the Rejection

Claims are automatically flagged in ClaimsFlow when a payer (insurance company) returns them with a denial code. You'll see a red "REJECTED" status on the claim detail page.

- Check the **Rejection Code** field—this indicates why the payer denied it
- Common codes: 42 (Missing EOB), 87 (Invalid Member ID), 156 (Coding Error), 203 (Out of Network)
- Document the code in the claim notes for tracking

## Step 2: Route to Appropriate Team

**For eligibility issues (codes 87, 91, 201):**
- Assign to Care Coordination team
- Tag in Slack: @care-coord-leads
- They verify member enrollment in CareBridge

**For coding/documentation issues (codes 42, 156, 178):**
- Assign to Claims Ops supervisor (currently Sarah Chen or Marcus Rodriguez)
- Note: If claim involves behavioral health codes, loop in our contracted coding auditor at External Coding Solutions

**For network/provider issues (codes 203, 267):**
- Contact Platform Engineering via Jira ticket
- They update provider network files in ClaimsFlow's backend

## Step 3: Gather Documentation

Pull the original claim submission from ClaimsFlow's document archive:
- Original claim form (CMS-1500 or 837 EDI file)
- Attached medical records or EOB
- Any prior correspondence with payer
- Member's current eligibility record from Workday integration

Save these to the claim's Confluence ticket (create one if missing, naming format: CLAIM-[Member ID]-[Date])

## Step 4: Correct and Resubmit

**For missing documents:** Attach missing EOB or medical record, then resubmit via ClaimsFlow's "Resubmit Claim" button.

**For coding errors:** Update the diagnosis/procedure codes in ClaimsFlow. Our coding guidelines are in Confluence under Claims Ops > Coding Standards v2.3. Resubmit after correction.

**For eligibility:** Verify member's plan effective date and coverage tier in CareBridge. If outdated, update Workday and sync (this happens automatically nightly, or manually via "Force Sync" in CareBridge admin panel).

## Step 5: Track and Follow Up

- Update claim status in ClaimsFlow to "RESUBMITTED"
- Create a Jira ticket: Project "CLAIMS," issue type "Rejection Follow-up"
- Assign to yourself with due date 5 business days out
- Add payer reference number and rejection code to ticket description

## Step 6: Verify Resolution

After 5 days, check ClaimsFlow for updated claim status. Payers typically respond within 3-7 business days.

- If approved: Close Jira ticket, mark claim "PAID"
- If rejected again: Escalate to Sarah Chen and create new follow-up ticket

## Escalation

Contact the Claims Ops manager (Sarah Chen, sarah.chen@meridian.local) if:
- Same claim rejected twice
- Rejection code is unclear or undocumented
- Payer is unresponsive after 10 days

# Creating a New Report in PulseBoard

## Overview

PulseBoard is our primary reporting dashboard for claims, care coordination metrics, and operational KPIs. This runbook covers the process for creating a new standard report. For custom SQL queries, contact Data & Analytics.

## Prerequisites

- Active PulseBoard account with Editor role (request via Workday IT Portal)
- Access to the data source you're reporting on (ClaimsFlow, CareBridge, or TimeTrax)
- Confluence page documenting your report requirements (template: [Report Planning Template](https://confluence.meridian.local/display/ANALYTICS/Report+Planning))
- Approval from your team lead

## Step-by-Step Instructions

### 1. Log into PulseBoard

Navigate to `pulseboards.meridian.local` and authenticate with your Meridian credentials.

### 2. Create a New Report

- Click **+ New Report** (top right)
- Enter a report name following this format: `[Team]-[Metric]-[Frequency]` 
  - Example: `ClaimsOps-DenialRate-Weekly`
- Select your primary data source from the dropdown (ClaimsFlow, CareBridge, TimeTrax, or Workday)
- Click **Create**

### 3. Configure Data Fields

- In the **Fields** panel (left sidebar), select which metrics to display
- Common fields for Claims Ops: Claim ID, Status, Denial Reason, Processing Time, Provider
- Common fields for Care Coordination: Member ID, Intervention Type, Outcome, Date Assigned
- Drag fields into the **Columns** section to order them
- Click the filter icon next to each field to set default filters (e.g., Status = "Processed" only)

### 4. Set Visualization Type

- Click **Visualization** tab
- Choose your chart type: Table, Bar Chart, Line Chart, or Heatmap
- For trend analysis, use Line Chart with date grouping set to "Weekly" or "Monthly"
- For comparison, use Bar Chart with categorical grouping (e.g., by Provider or Denial Reason)

### 5. Apply Filters and Date Range

- Click **Filters** (top toolbar)
- Add date range: select **Date Range Type** → choose "Last 30 Days" or set custom dates
- Add additional filters as needed (e.g., Claims Ops team reports should filter Department = "Claims Operations")

# How a Claim Moves Through ClaimsFlow: End-to-End

## Overview

ClaimsFlow processes all incoming insurance claims for our partner networks. A typical claim takes 8-12 business days from submission to either approval or denial. This document outlines each stage.

## Stage 1: Intake & Initial Validation (Day 1)

Claims arrive via three channels: EDI feeds from partner systems, our web portal, or manual uploads. The system performs basic validation:

- Required fields present (member ID, provider NPI, DOS, service code)
- Date of service not older than 180 days
- Member exists in our database
- Duplicate detection against last 90 days

Invalid claims are rejected with specific error codes and marked "INTAKE_FAILED" in ClaimsFlow. Valid claims move to the queue and are assigned a Claim ID (format: CLM-YYYYMM-#####).

## Stage 2: Pre-Adjudication Rules Engine (Day 2-3)

Our rules engine runs ~47 automated checks, including:

- Benefit coverage verification (checking CareBridge for active enrollment)
- Network provider validation
- Bundling rules (e.g., lab panels must bundle under one code)
- Frequency limits (e.g., preventive screenings per calendar year)
- Age/gender edits (pediatric services for adults, etc.)

Claims that pass all rules are marked "RULES_CLEARED." Those with violations are flagged for Claims Ops review or auto-denied based on severity.

## Stage 3: Manual Review (Day 4-6)

Complex claims requiring human judgment go to Claims Ops team. Our current SLA is 2 business days per claim. Reviewers use the ClaimsFlow dashboard to:

- Pull member eligibility from Workday integration
- Review clinical documentation attachments
- Compare against plan-specific policies (stored in Confluence)
- Consult with Care Coordination via CareBridge if needed

Reviewers either approve, deny, or request more information from the provider.

## Stage 4: Determination & Communication (Day 7-10)

Approved claims are priced using our fee schedule and sent to accounting. Denials are logged with reason codes (e.g., "NOT_COVERED," "FREQUENCY_EXCEEDED"). Both are communicated to providers via EDI or email.

Members receive an Explanation of Benefits (EOB) generated by PulseBoard and mailed within 5 business days.

# CareBridge & ClaimsFlow Integration

## What is CareBridge?

CareBridge is our care coordination platform that manages patient workflows across episodes of care. Built in 2021, it tracks everything from initial patient intake through discharge, including provider assignments, care plans, and patient touchpoints. The system currently manages ~45,000 active patient records across our network.

CareBridge is owned and maintained by the **Care Coordination team**, with Platform Engineering providing backend support.

## Key CareBridge Functions

- **Patient Intake**: Captures demographics, insurance info, and clinical flags
- **Care Plan Management**: Assigns care coordinators and tracks interventions
- **Provider Network**: Maintains our contracted provider directory (~2,800 providers)
- **Touchpoint Logging**: Records calls, visits, and patient interactions
- **Discharge Planning**: Manages transitions to post-acute care or primary care

## How CareBridge Connects to ClaimsFlow

When a patient is enrolled in CareBridge, their care journey eventually generates claims. Here's how the two systems talk:

### Data Flow (High Level)

1. **Patient Enrollment** → CareBridge creates a patient record with insurance details
2. **Care Events** → Interventions logged in CareBridge (e.g., "diabetes education session")
3. **Claim Generation** → ClaimsFlow pulls eligible events and creates claim line items
4. **Claim Status** → ClaimsFlow updates are pushed back to CareBridge for visibility

### Technical Details

CareBridge sends **daily batch files** to ClaimsFlow at 2:00 AM EST via SFTP. The file format is CSV and includes:

- Patient ID (MRN)
- Service date
- Service code (CPT/HCPCS)
- Provider NPI
- Units of service
- Authorization reference (if applicable)

**File naming convention**: `carebridge_claims_YYYYMMDD.csv`

ClaimsFlow processes these files through our standard validation rules and flags issues in the **CareBridge Claims Integration** Jira board (maintained by Claims Ops).

### Common Integration Issues

- **Missing authorization numbers**: CareBridge sometimes doesn't capture auth IDs before discharge. This causes claim rejections in ClaimsFlow.
- **Provider NPI mismatches**: Provider data drifts between systems. We reconcile quarterly.
- **Duplicate claims**: If a care event is logged twice in CareBridge, ClaimsFlow may create duplicate line items. The Claims Ops team manually deduplicates these.

# Common Meridian Acronyms

This page defines acronyms you'll encounter across Meridian Health Partners. When in doubt, ask in #general-slack or check Confluence.

## Claims & Operations

**EOB** - Explanation of Benefits. When a claim is processed through ClaimsFlow, the EOB is generated for the member within 24-48 hours.

**ERA** - Electronic Remittance Advice. Payers send us ERAs daily; the Claims Ops team reconciles these in ClaimsFlow by 5 PM EST.

**CCLF** - Claim-level Cost and Utilization File. We submit CCLFs to CMS quarterly for our Medicare Advantage contracts. Data & Analytics owns this in PulseBoard.

**MIPS** - Merit-based Incentive Payment System. Our providers track MIPS scores; Care Coordination uses CareBridge to monitor progress against our Q4 targets.

**NAP** - Network Adequacy Plan. Updated annually in January; Platform Engineering maintains NAP data in our provider directory system.

## Care Coordination

**PCP** - Primary Care Physician. When members enroll, CareBridge auto-assigns them to a PCP based on geography and availability.

**TCM** - Transitional Care Management. After hospital discharge, our TCM nurses use CareBridge to schedule 14-day follow-ups; 87% completion rate as of November.

**BH** - Behavioral Health. Our BH team coordinates with external partners; referrals are logged in CareBridge with a 3-day callback target.

**SDOH** - Social Determinants of Health. CareBridge now flags SDOH risk factors. In 2024, we identified 12,400 members with housing instability.

## Technology & Operations

**SLA** - Service Level Agreement. ClaimsFlow has a 99.2% uptime SLA; Platform Engineering tracks this on PulseBoard every hour.

**SFTP** - Secure File Transfer Protocol. Payers submit claim files to our SFTP server nightly; automated scripts in GitHub validate these files at 2 AM.

**ETL** - Extract, Transform, Load. Data & Analytics runs six ETL jobs daily to populate PulseBoard with fresh metrics from our database.

**MFA** - Multi-Factor Authentication. All employees must enable MFA in Workday per our 2023 security mandate.

**RTO/RPO** - Recovery Time Objective / Recovery Point Objective. Our disaster recovery plan targets RTO of 4 hours and RPO of 1 hour for all critical systems.

## HR & Scheduling

**PTO** - Paid Time Off. TimeTrax integrates with Workday; submit PTO requests at least 14 days in advance.

**FTE** - Full-Time Equivalent. Our Claims Ops team operates at 47 FTE; HR uses this metric for budget planning.

**OT** - Overtime. During March peak season, Care Coordination staff may accrue OT; TimeTrax flags this automatically for approval.

## General

**QA** - Quality Assurance. Every 50th claim processed in ClaimsFlow is pulled for QA review by a second Claims Ops analyst.

**UAT** - User Acceptance Testing. Before any ClaimsFlow release, Claims Ops runs UAT for 5 business days in our staging environment.

**ROI** - Return on Investment. CareBridge's ROI was 2.3x in 2023 based on readmission reduction alone.

# On-Call Basics for Platform Engineering

## Overview

All Platform Engineering team members rotate through on-call duty. The schedule is managed in PagerDuty and syncs with our Slack channel #platform-oncall. Each rotation is one week, starting Monday at 9 AM EST.

On-call engineers are responsible for responding to production incidents across ClaimsFlow, CareBridge, PulseBoard, and TimeTrax. Response time SLA is 15 minutes for critical incidents (P1), 30 minutes for high priority (P2).

## Getting Started

**Before your rotation:**
- Review the runbook in Confluence: "Platform Engineering Runbooks" (last updated March 2023—some sections may reference old infrastructure)
- Ensure you have VPN access, AWS console access, and GitHub permissions
- Add your phone number and email to your PagerDuty profile
- Test your notification settings (phone calls, SMS, Slack)

**During your rotation:**
- Check #platform-oncall each morning for handoff notes
- Keep your laptop within reach during business hours
- For after-hours, you can be on-call from home but should be reachable

## Incident Response Flow

1. **Alert received** → PagerDuty notifies you via phone/SMS/Slack
2. **Acknowledge** → Click the acknowledge button in PagerDuty within 5 minutes
3. **Assess** → Check PulseBoard for error rates and system status. Join the incident Slack channel (auto-created as #incident-XXXX)
4. **Escalate if needed** → After 10 minutes without progress on P1s, escalate to the secondary on-call engineer (see PagerDuty rotation)
5. **Resolve** → Update #platform-oncall with resolution details and post-incident follow-up link

## Common Issues & Quick Fixes

**ClaimsFlow API timeouts:** Usually caused by database connection pool exhaustion. SSH into claims-prod-1 and check `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pg_stat_activity;` Check Jira ticket CLAIMSFLOW-2847 for full troubleshooting steps.

**CareBridge data sync delays:** Restart the sync service via Kubernetes: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/carebridge-sync -n production`. Takes about 3 minutes.

**PulseBoard dashboard slow:** Clear Redis cache: `redis-cli -h pulseBoard-redis FLUSHDB`. Coordinate with Data & Analytics if this is recurring.

**TimeTrax scheduler not triggering:** Check GitHub Actions logs in the timetrax-scheduler repo. Often a failed dependency update. Rollback to previous commit if needed.

## Handoff & Documentation

At the end of your rotation:
- Post a summary in #platform-oncall with incident counts and any ongoing issues
- Update the runbook if you discovered new fixes
- Schedule a brief 15-minute handoff call with your replacement (use Calendly: link in Confluence)

## Escalation

- **Technical questions:** Message #platform-engineering or tag @marcus-devops
- **Customer impact:** Notify #claims-ops or #care-coordination team leads immediately
- **Multiple systems down:** Contact VP of Engineering (currently Sarah Chen) and page the secondary on-call

## Time Off & Swaps

Request time off in PagerDuty at least 2 weeks in advance. Find your own swap or contact @platform-team-leads in Slack. Do not skip your rotation without coverage.
